strategy.summary: cartTotal in src/cart.js prices the cart: bulk 10% off at 10+ items (summed across lines), SAVE5 coupon after bulk discount with a $0 floor, unknown coupons refused, and $4.99 shipping unless discounted goods reach $50 (empty cart free). Unit tests with Vitest on cartTotal prove each rule at its boundaries. Reading the code shows bulkDiscount uses `> BULK_THRESHOLD`, so exactly 10 items gets no discount — a suspected defect against AC1, kept as an expected failure.
inScope: cartTotal, bulkDiscount behaviour via cartTotal in src/cart.js
assumptions: Prices are in dollars as numbers; cartTotal returns a number rounded to cents.
Coupon codes are case-sensitive: only exact 'SAVE5' is accepted (code uses Object.hasOwn on {SAVE5}).
openQuestions: The refusal is an Error whose only distinguishing data is the message 'Unknown coupon: <code>'; there is no error code. Tests assert the message contains the submitted code.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cart with 10 or more items in total (sum of line quantities) gets 10% off its subtotal.
SAVE5 takes $5 off after the bulk discount; goods never cost less than $0; any other coupon code is refused with an error.
Shipping is free when goods after discounts are $50 or more, otherwise $4.99; an empty cart costs nothing.

defects.title: Cart of exactly 10 items gets no bulk discount
defects.description: AC1: a cart with 10 or more items in total gets 10% off. bulkDiscount (src/cart.js:22) uses `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD`, so exactly 10 items gets no discount. Expected cartTotal of lines {10×4},{10×6} = 90; actual 100. Fix: use >=.
defects.evidence: TC1 marked it.fails passes (i.e. the assertion toBe(90) fails); src/cart.js:22 `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD`.
